original_question: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T112(n+2, 2n) equals the number of royal paths in a lattice of order n for every n >= 1?
target_in_paper: Section 7 (Both stones, two kinds of bones), Problem 13: whether T_{112}(n + 2, 2n) is the number of royal paths in a lattice of order n for all n >= 1. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct counting function T_{112}, the correct tile-allowance regime (both stone orientations and exactly two bone orientations), the correct benzel family (n + 2, 2n), the correct comparison class (royal paths), and the correct quantifier n >= 1. It is essentially Problem 13 stated in your own words. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the question should define the (a,b)-benzel itself; in the paper this is the union of unit hexagonal cells whose barycentric centers (i,j,k) in Z^3 satisfy i + j + k = 1 and -(a - 1) <= j - i, k - j, i - k <= b - 1. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

It should define T_{ijk}(a,b) using the paper's notation: T_{ijk}(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel by translates of the five prototiles, where the right stone is allowed iff i = 1, the left stone is allowed iff j = 1, and exactly k of the three bone prototiles are allowed. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

For T_{112}, the paper's setup uses symmetry to make the count depend only on how many bone orientations are allowed, not on which particular two are chosen. Making that implicit symmetry explicit improves stand-alone clarity. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

The phrase royal paths in a lattice of order n should be identified with OEIS sequence A006319, exactly as in Problem 13. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
refined_question: For integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, let the (a,b)-benzel be the union of unit hexagonal cells in the triangular grid whose barycentric centers (i,j,k) in Z^3 satisfy i + j + k = 1 and -(a - 1) <= j - i, k - j, i - k <= b - 1. Let T_{112}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of this region by translates of the right stone, the left stone, and any two of the three bone prototiles. Is it true that, for every integer n >= 1, T_{112}(n + 2, 2n) equals the number of royal paths in a lattice of order n (OEIS A006319)? ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Problem 13, not the nearby central-diagonal Problems 8-11 or the all-prototiles questions in Section 8. The paper's exact nearby context defining benzels, prototiles, and T_{ijk}(a,b) appears in Section 1, while the exact conjectural statement appears in Section 7 as Problem 13. No additional hypotheses, asymptotic clauses, algebraic ambient structures, or alternate equivalent formulations are attached to this problem in the paper itself. ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))
